content.thinking:
I'm going through the claims one by one. The still-at-risk point is a reading of the record: by 12:53:10 the service hadn't recovered and no one had been paged. The symptom is that io-shop requests were failing, which the HighErrorRate alert backs up by showing the error rate above threshold. Now I'm checking the causal chain, starting with that same alert as the first link.

I'm weighing whether "not routed to anyone on call" is actually supported, since the record only shows nobody was paged and no on-call incident was linked, not why. I'm also checking the what-if about the incident ending in an escalation with nobody on it, which the record backs up with the escalation event.

I'm checking the remaining claims about the investigation's gaps: Argus couldn't read io-shop's per-minute metrics, no log lines came back for the period before the alert, and it couldn't tell where the three running replicas were placed, even though the platform reported no pods.

content.text:
I found no claims to flag in the document; all 11 claims I judged are supported by the record. Action items weren't judged, and the document has no went_wrong field, so the placement check didn't apply.

One borderline case: contributing factor 1 says the alert "was not routed to anyone on call." The record only says no on-call incident was linked and nobody was paged. It doesn't say why. I counted this as a fair restatement rather than a new claim about the cause, but it's the call most open to disagreement.
